data.narrative:
Graphyte is a Series A-stage climate and energy technology company founded by Barclay Rogers that has raised $57M to date. The valuation framework draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable firms: 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private entities including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the private comparable set lacks sufficient depth at Graphyte's stage and valuation tier to enable traditional peer-median analysis; only one method proved applicable to this dataset.

The stage-progression method was applied as the primary valuation driver. Using the $57M total raised as a proxy for current implied valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $114M. This methodology assumes Graphyte will progress to Series B or equivalent within a reasonable timeframe and capture the customary valuation uplift associated with that transition. No peer-median triangulation was feasible given the absence of three or more same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient data density.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $97M to $131M, centered on a median of $114M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression result. The primary uncertainty remains the scarcity of narrow-stage peer data in Climate & Energy; broader sector comparables exist but would introduce material sector-heterogeneity bias. Subsequent valuation updates should incorporate additional Series A or Series B Climate & Energy closings to strengthen the peer-median approach.
